A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same self-consistency scaling analysis and Blend-ASC method. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM sampling and simulation results, including margin–error correlations, dataset scaling curves, and comparisons of adaptive sampling methods.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds batching sensitivity experiments and a computational-overhead measurement.

M1.justification: Section 5 adds procedural adaptations that select several questions for parallel generation and process arriving queries in independently budgeted groups. The underlying ASC/PPR ranking blend and the 16-times-average sampling cap remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The existing benchmark coverage, including GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, and GPQA-Diamond, is retained. The batched-query experiment adds a simulated streaming scenario in which queries are serviced in separate groups instead of being jointly available as one dataset.

E2.justification: SC, fixed allocation, ASC, and PPR-1v1 remain the evaluated comparators. The complete comparisons from v1 Figure 7 are retained in v2 Appendix F despite reduced comparator displays in the main-text overview. Newly discussed reflection methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 8 introduces batch sizes of 1–32 and query-group counts of 1–16, evaluated against SC at 64 and 128 samples across four temperatures. The temperature-0.8 aggregate savings also change from averaging per-case ratios to values consistent with dividing the SC budget by mean sample counts. Existing generation and simulation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new extended analysis tests sensitivity to parallel generation batch size and the fragmentation of queries into separately processed groups. Figure 8 provides evidence of relatively stable sample efficiency under both variations; these analyses are absent from v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 runs per model–benchmark pair for ASC and PPR-1v1 and retain the existing shaded performance plots. No new seed information, confidence-interval methodology, significance testing, or repeated-run count is introduced.

E6.justification: At temperature 0.8, Blend-ASC's aggregate savings change from 6.78×/6.92× to 5.33×/4.29× for SC@64/128, while all corresponding per-case sample counts remain identical. Baseline aggregates also change. v2 adds batching results, a 1.8-second overhead measurement, and a p1−p2-labeled synthetic distribution curve in Figure 3.

T1.justification: Appendix C revises the tail-pooling proof, extends Lemma 5's lower-bound argument, and corrects formulas in Lemmas 7–8. However, Proposition 2 changes the D3 density exponent from n−1/2 to −n−1/2, contradicting v2 Lemma 8. Corollary 4 replaces the explicit LB(δ,q) denominator with Ω(log(1/δ)) inside an exact limiting ratio. These are localized revisions within the retained theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction reduce the headline savings claim from 6.8× to 4.8× and add explicit batching support. The introduction expands the claimed first theoretical coverage from dynamic allocation to both fixed and dynamic allocation. The principal scaling-law and Blend-ASC contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly excludes tasks without natural majority-vote aggregation, including open-ended generation. It replaces the earlier answer-concentration explanation of multiple-choice behavior with discussion of difficulties obtaining tight bounds for misaligned questions. It also adds deployment interpretations and qualifications concerning extensions beyond majority voting.

D1.justification: v2 supplies operational instructions for batching, reports computational overhead, and identifies Language Model Eval Harness, PyTorch, and vLLM as supporting software. Appendix B's existing fixed- and dynamic-allocation implementation details are substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature on preference optimization, consistency and reliability, and reflection methods such as mirror-consistency, SelfCheck, and self-contrast. It positions sequential reflection as complementary to parallel sampling and adds dataset, model, and software references. The central positioning around mode estimation and voting theory remains.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes Section 3 around assumptions and the main result, separates Blend-ASC into Section 4.3, and revises contribution bullets, terminology, explanatory paragraphs, and future work. Author and affiliation information also changes. The overall section sequence and much of the narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensively redesigned figures and captions. v2 combines the original overview and SC illustration, adds an algorithm diagram and batching plots, corrects margin-density axes, and relocates the full performance grid to Appendix F. The temperature-1.0 table remains available in Appendix F after leaving the main text.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful batching evidence, clarifies applicability, makes aggregate savings consistent across temperatures, and corrects appendix formulas. However, its revised Proposition 2 contradicts Lemma 8, and Corollary 4 replaces a defined normalization with imprecise asymptotic notation. These gains coexist with regressions in central theoretical statements, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
